text:
oliver: quick question  compact service chart in figma shows throughput (req/s) + p95 (ms) together. space is tiny. do we allow dual axes?
sam: avoid dual axes if possible. users misread scales.
nina: agree. three options: stacked mini-rows, normalized percent axis, or single axis + unit chips and hover details.
oliver: ops wants ms visible at glance. stacking eats vertical space. normalized hides absolute numbers.
sam: what about single axis with small unit chip per series and a persistent data button that opens table with raw units? keeps canvas small and accessible.
nina: outliers: large latency spikes will still blow scale. option: visual clamp at 99th pct + faint dashed cap line and shaded outlier markers. tooltip explains "values above X capped for display".
oliver: smoothing interactions? smoothing should be computed on raw values (rolling median) and we render smoothed line over the capped raw points so trend holds.
sam: accessibility: include hidden summary text under chart: "Throughput (requests per second) and 95th percentile latency (milliseconds). Open data table for exact values." screen reader reads full-unit words.
dev-bot: summary: "Prefer capped visualization (99th pct) with outlier markers; avoid dual-axis; add unit chips and persistent data button; smoothing computed on raw then rendered on capped visuals; include SR-friendly hidden summary."
oliver: thanks  i'll update the mock with cap-line and data button.
